stem: On a trusted laptop, you want to authenticate once and then reuse your credentials in later Python sessions without pasting your API key each time. Which approach matches the documented workflow?

options.text: Store the backend name in `save_account` so the recommended backend is reused automatically.
Pass `token=` and `instance=` to `QiskitRuntimeService()` in every script; the API key is deliberately never stored on the laptop between Python sessions.
Call `QiskitRuntimeService.save_account(token="<api-key>", instance="<CRN>")` once; later `QiskitRuntimeService()` loads it.
Call `QiskitRuntimeService.login()` with your IBM id and password.
Call `QiskitRuntimeService.save_account(api_key="<api-key>", instance="<CRN>")` once; the token keyword was renamed to `api_key` on IBM Quantum Platform.
Call `QiskitRuntimeService(token="<api-key>").save()` after the first successful connection, which typically writes the account file for you.

explanation.correct: `QiskitRuntimeService.save_account(token=..., instance=...)` saves credentials to disk once (recommended only in a trusted environment). Later, `QiskitRuntimeService()` with no arguments loads the saved default account, so you never paste the key again.

distractors.A: `save_account` stores authentication credentials, not a backend choice; you still select a backend (for example with `least_busy`) at run time.
distractors.B: Explicit per-script credentials are one option, but credentials CAN be persisted with `save_account`; nothing prevents writing them to disk on a trusted machine.
distractors.D: There is no `login()` method that takes an id and password; authentication uses an API key/token, optionally saved with `save_account`.
distractors.E: The parameter is still `token=`, whatever the web console calls the string you paste into it. `save_account` has no `api_key` parameter, so this raises `TypeError` before anything is written to disk.
distractors.F: There is no `save()` method on the service — persisting credentials is a class-level operation, `QiskitRuntimeService.save_account(...)`, and it does not require a live connection first.

provenance.notes: meta-pattern fix pass: length/stem-echo/absolute calibration (s4) — trimmed correct C, lengthened+hedged distractors (length/stem-echo/absolute-tell fix). | pool wave: +E (save_account(api_key=...)), +F (service.save() persists the account)
